_comment: Built-in screening presets. Each preset defines filters and sort criteria.

_filter_keys.above_50ma: Must be trading above the 50-day moving average (true/false)
_filter_keys.above_200ma: Must be trading above the 200-day moving average (true/false)
_filter_keys.near_52w_low: Within N% of the 52-week low (number, e.g. 10 = within 10%)
_filter_keys.revenue_growth_min: Minimum YoY revenue growth as decimal (e.g. 0.20 = 20%)
_filter_keys.earnings_growth_min: Minimum YoY earnings growth as decimal

value.description: Classic value investing screen — low P/E, low P/B, profitable companies trading at a discount to fundamentals.
value.learning_note: Value investors (like Warren Buffett) look for companies that are 'cheap' relative to their earnings and assets. P/E < 15 means you're paying less than $15 for every $1 of earnings.

momentum.description: Stocks with strong price momentum — above their 50-day MA, high relative volume, and recent outperformance.
momentum.learning_note: Momentum investing is based on the idea that stocks trending up tend to keep trending up (at least short-term). High relative volume means big money is moving in.

dividend.description: Income-focused screen — stocks with dividend yields above 3% and solid earnings to support the payout.
dividend.learning_note: Dividend yield = annual dividend / stock price. A 3% yield on a $100 stock means $3/year per share. Look for sustainable payouts (not companies paying more than they earn).

growth.description: High-growth companies with accelerating revenue and earnings — often higher P/E but worth it if growth is real.
growth.learning_note: Growth investors pay a premium today for future earnings. Revenue growth > 20% YoY suggests the company is taking market share. Watch out for 'growth traps' — companies that grow revenue but never turn profitable.

oversold.description: Beaten-down stocks near their 52-week lows — potential bounce candidates (but could also keep falling).
oversold.learning_note: Contrarian investing: buying what everyone else is selling. Near 52-week lows can mean opportunity OR a value trap. Always ask WHY a stock fell before buying the dip.

large_cap.description: The biggest, most stable companies (market cap > $100B). Less volatility, battle-tested businesses.
large_cap.learning_note: Large caps are the 'blue chips' — companies like Apple, Microsoft, Johnson & Johnson. Lower risk than small caps but also lower growth potential.

volume_spike.description: Unusual volume today — stocks with 2x+ average daily volume. Something is happening.
volume_spike.learning_note: Volume spikes often precede or accompany big price moves. Could be earnings, news, activist investor, acquisition rumor — always dig into WHY volume is elevated.
